newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Benin president's abandoned Boeing to become a bar.
newsitem.headline: Benin president's abandoned Boeing to become a bar.

text.p: A customized Boeing 707, believed to have been owned by Mathieu Kerekou, a former president of the west African state of Benin, and abandoned in Belgium's Ostend airport seven years ago, has been given a new lease of life...as a novelty restaurant.

Ronny Lauwereins, assistant head of airport security, said the luxuriously fitted airliner had been sold to a group of businessmen and would be towed to the Dutch province of Limburg where it will be turned into a bar and grill for the jet set.

"In 1989 the plane should have gone to (Britain's) Stansted airport for a refit. But there was a waiting list and, as parking fees were cheaper here than there, it was flown to Ostend," he said by telephone.
"However, there was then a change of president and the new one didn't know the plane was parked here," he added.
Over the past seven years the rusting Boeing has clocked up unpaid parking fees of 13 million francs ($370,000).
As part of the deal between the Benin government, the Flemish regional government and the airport, Benin will only have to pay a token parking fee.
"The plane will be gone from here by the end of May," Lauwereins said.
